s0102.literal: First the names and numbers must be obtained along with their charges, and then we shall convene again.
s0102.idiomatic: First obtain the prisoners' names, their number, and the charges against them, then convene again.

s0103.literal: " The Court Tribunal supervisor Shen Zhongyou then submitted a list, saying that since the new regulations there had been one Shou Yu'er convicted of killing Shou Hui, and eight men including Liu Leike convicted of stealing horses and taking household members north across the border; interrogated under the law to the time limit, none confessed.
s0103.idiomatic: " Court tribunal supervisor Shen Zhongyou then listed cases since the new rules: one Shou Yu'er for killing Shou Hui, and Liu Leike and seven others for stealing horses and taking dependents north; all were interrogated under law to the time limit without confessing.

s0104.literal: Liu Daoshuo was convicted of seven counts of theft; interrogated under the law, he confessed within two days from start to finish.
s0104.idiomatic: Liu Daoshuo was convicted of seven thefts; under legal interrogation he confessed within two days.

s0105.literal: Chen Manman was convicted of being sent to seal stores and Afu accepting money; before the session was up he confessed.
s0105.idiomatic: Chen Manman was convicted of sealing stores on commission and Afu taking bribes; he confessed before the session ended.

s0106.literal: Hongzheng argued: "In great and small cases alike one must proceed by the facts, speak straight and follow the Five Hearings, and test truth and falsehood—how can one wholly rely on beating under examination to fix guilt?
s0106.idiomatic: Hongzheng argued, "Cases great and small must follow the facts, apply the Five Hearings, and test truth and falsehood—how can guilt be fixed wholly by torture in examination?

s0107.literal: Moreover the seasons for interrogation under torture are not an ancient institution; only in recent times has this method appeared.
s0107.idiomatic: Moreover the hours for interrogation under torture are not ancient; only in recent times has this method existed.

s0108.literal: From the afternoon drum to the second watch—can ordinary men endure it?
s0108.idiomatic: From the afternoon drum to the second watch—is that something ordinary men can endure?

s0109.literal: Hence under heavy fetters and on the brink of collapse, none fails to submit, and many are wrongly convicted.
s0109.idiomatic: Hence under heavy fetters and on the brink of collapse, none fails to submit, and wrongful convictions are many.

s0110.literal: Morning and evening sessions with equal clepsydra counts, weighed forward and back, hit the mean for the matter.
s0110.idiomatic: Morning and evening sessions with equal clepsydra counts, weighed together, strike the right balance.

s0111.literal: If one says shortening the earlier period makes the truly guilty refuse to submit, then extending the season would leave no false confessions.
s0111.idiomatic: If shortening the earlier period makes the truly guilty refuse to confess, extending the hours would leave no false confessions.

s0112.literal: Moreover what men can bear differs in strength, and how men set their minds also follows many paths.
s0112.idiomatic: Moreover endurance differs by strength, and men's resolve follows many paths.

s0113.literal: Take for example Guan Gao, flogged, branded, and burned until no part of his body was whole, [8] or Dai Jiu, smoked with needles to the utmost yet unshaken in distress—what has that to do with the length of the hours or whether interrogation is harsh or mild?
s0113.idiomatic: Guan Gao was flogged, branded, and burned until no part of his body was whole [8]; Dai Jiu was smoked with needles to the utmost yet would not yield—what has that to do with the length of the hours or the severity of interrogation?

s0114.literal: Rather than kill the innocent, better to miss punishing the guilty; when guilt is doubtful, lean light; when merit is doubtful, lean heavy: such is the clear law the ancient sage kings handed down.
s0114.idiomatic: Rather than kill the innocent, better to let the guilty go unpunished; when guilt is doubtful, lean light; when merit is doubtful, lean heavy—such is the clear law the ancient sage kings handed down.

s0115.literal: I hold that following Fan Quan's established regulations is acceptable for the matter.
s0115.idiomatic: I hold that following Fan Quan's regulations is acceptable.

s0116.literal: " Attendant Sheng Quan argued: "The new regulations of the Ministry of Justice Fan Quan and the clear argument of Minister Zhou Hongzheng both accord with the intent of the Yu canon to lean light and the Yin hymn to spread rectitude.
s0116.idiomatic: " Attendant Sheng Quan argued, "Fan Quan's new regulations at the ministry of justice and Minister Zhou Hongzheng's clear argument both accord with the Yu canon to lean light and the Yin hymn to spread rectitude.

s0117.literal: I have examined the list of Court Tribunal supervisor Shen Zhongyou and others: since the new regulations there have been eleven cases in all; ten were interrogated, and only one confessed.
s0117.idiomatic: I have examined Shen Zhongyou's list: since the new rules there have been eleven cases; ten were interrogated, and only one confessed.

s0118.literal: I hold that for prisoners tainted with guilt, prison officials should clearly argue and analyze and exhaust the facts of the case.
s0118.idiomatic: I hold that for prisoners tainted with guilt, officials should argue the case clearly and exhaust the facts.

s0119.literal: If the crime is doubtful, they should themselves open review and divide judgment, and by good fortune not interrogate at random;
s0119.idiomatic: If the crime is doubtful, they should open review and divide judgment, and not interrogate at random;

s0120.literal: if the crime is clearly proved, only then may they open review and set interrogation;
s0120.idiomatic: if the crime is clearly proved, only then may they set interrogation;

s0121.literal: then crooked and straight have their division, and mercy in punishment follows reason.
s0121.idiomatic: then guilt and innocence are distinguished, and mercy in punishment follows reason.

s0122.literal: Fan Quan now in his memorial cites Han law, saying: 'For capital crimes and removal from the registers, when the proof of guilt is clear and beating under examination has already been applied yet the accused still conceals and will not submit, the case should be listed and sent up.'
s0122.idiomatic: Fan Quan's memorial cites Han law: "For capital crimes and removal from the registers, when proof is clear and beating under examination has been applied yet the accused still conceals and will not submit, the case should be listed and sent up."

s0123.literal: Du Yu's commentary says: 'Listed up means the clearly proved circumstances, listing the intent to conceal.'
s0123.idiomatic: Du Yu's commentary says, "Listed up means the clearly proved circumstances, listing the intent to conceal."

s0124.literal: I find the old regulations severe: of a hundred, one did not confess; the new regulations are lenient: of ten, nine did not confess. Comparing the two texts, leniency and severity truly differ, yet 'listed and sent up' is nowhere revised.
s0124.idiomatic: The old rules were severe: one in a hundred did not confess; the new rules are lenient: nine in ten did not confess. The two texts differ in leniency and severity, yet "listed and sent up" is nowhere revised.

s0125.literal: I hold that the matter should be referred to the codex office to examine further the text 'listed and sent up.'
s0125.idiomatic: I hold the matter should go to the codex office to examine further the phrase "listed and sent up."

s0126.literal: " Zhu argued: "Interrogation at night is easy to abuse in urgency or slackness; using the day clepsydra as well is acceptable for the matter.
s0126.idiomatic: " Zhu argued, "Night interrogation is easy to abuse; using the day clepsydra as well is acceptable.

s0127.literal: But clepsydra periods differ in length between past and present. In the Han shu on calendrics and the clepsydra classics of He Chengtian, Zu Chongzhi, and father and son Hui, from the gate drum to the lower drum and from the afternoon drum to the gate drum are all thirteen marks, alike in winter and summer through the four seasons.
s0127.idiomatic: But clepsydra periods differ between past and present. In the Han shu on calendrics and the clepsydra classics of He Chengtian, Zu Chongzhi, and the Hui father and son, from gate drum to lower drum and from afternoon drum to gate drum are all thirteen marks, alike through the four seasons.

s0128.literal: If the day was long or short, the division fell before or after midday.
s0128.idiomatic: If the day was long or short, the division fell before or after midday.

s0129.literal: Now the revised clepsydra of late Liang is used: after the lower drum the short and long are divided; on the summer solstice each has seventeen marks, on the winter solstice each has twelve marks.
s0129.idiomatic: Now the revised clepsydra of late Liang is used: after the lower drum the short and long are divided; on the summer solstice each period has seventeen marks, on the winter solstice twelve.

s0130.literal: I bow to receive the imperial order: the marks are the same as in the edict; checking one day's marks they are indeed equal, yet use through the four seasons is not equal. The Court Tribunal's present memorial, because the time marks were short and cramped,
s0130.idiomatic: I bow to receive the imperial order: the marks match the edict; checking one day's marks they are indeed equal, yet use through the four seasons is not equal. The court tribunal's memorial says that because the time marks were too short,

s0133.literal: [9] My intent is to remove the obscurity of night interrogation and follow the clarity of the day clepsydra, weighing between past and present and harmonizing the meaning of the two clepsydras, setting aside the fewer marks of autumn and winter and following the long daylight of summer—regardless of cold or heat, all alike following the present summer solstice, interrogating morning and evening, seventeen marks each.
s0133.idiomatic: [9] My intent is to end night interrogation and use the day clepsydra, weighing past and present and harmonizing both systems, setting aside autumn and winter's fewer marks and following summer's long daylight—regardless of season, following the present summer solstice with seventeen marks each for morning and evening interrogation.

s0134.literal: Compared with the ancient clepsydra, then one session has four more marks than of old [1]; using the present clepsydra, the winter solstice has five more marks [10].
s0134.idiomatic: Compared with the ancient clepsydra, each session has four more marks than of old [1]; using the present clepsydra, the winter solstice has five more marks [10].

s0135.literal: Although at the winter solstice several marks encroach on night, that is precisely when days are shortest [11]; for the matter there is no doubt.
s0135.idiomatic: Although at the winter solstice several marks encroach on night, that is when days are shortest [11]; there is no difficulty in the matter.

s0136.literal: May the guilty not resist because the clepsydra is short, and prisoners not because of night
s0136.idiomatic: May the guilty not resist because the clepsydra is short, and prisoners not at night

s0138.literal: [er] incur false conviction [12]; seeking my humble view, I hold it acceptable.
s0138.idiomatic: [er] suffer false conviction [12]; in my humble view this is acceptable.

s0139.literal: " The assembly held that Fan Quan's former regulations should be followed. Emperor Gaozong said: "Attendant Shen's argument hits the mean; a broader discussion should be held.
s0139.idiomatic: " The assembly held that Fan Quan's former regulations should be followed. Emperor Gaozong said, "Attendant Shen's argument hits the mean; hold a broader discussion.

s0140.literal: " Left Assistant Minister Zong Yuanyao argued: "I find Attendant Shen's argument is not suddenly unlike Fan's; he precisely wishes to make the four seasons equal in their mark counts, and also weigh what is best to meet leniency and severity.
s0140.idiomatic: " Left assistant minister Zong Yuanyao argued, "Attendant Shen's argument does not suddenly diverge from Fan's; he wishes to equalize mark counts through the four seasons and weigh what best meets leniency and severity.

s0141.literal: Let it be sent back with the same memorial to the Revision Office to examine and amend the former regulations in detail.
s0141.idiomatic: Let the same memorial be sent back to the revision office to examine and amend the former regulations in detail.

s0142.literal: " Emperor Gaozong followed the matter and put it into effect.
s0142.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozong approved and put it into effect.

s0143.literal: Zhu died in the first year of Taijian, aged fifty-two.
s0143.idiomatic: Zhu died in year 1 of Taijian, aged fifty-two.

s0144.literal: Qi Ji, styled Gongwen, was a native of Yanguan in Wu commandery.
s0144.idiomatic: Qi Ji, styled Gongwen, was from Yanguan in Wu commandery.

s0145.literal: His grandfather Xian was Qi Supervisor of Attendants.
s0145.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian was Qi supervisor of attendants.

s0146.literal: His father Ba was Liang Central Army Major in the Prince of Linhe's household.
s0146.idiomatic: His father Ba was Liang central army major in the Prince of Linhe's household.

s0147.literal: Ji from youth was clever; he traveled to study in the capital and received the Three Rites from Erudite Assistant Liu Wenshao; within a year or two he had the great principles largely in hand.
s0147.idiomatic: Ji was clever from youth; he studied in the capital under erudite assistant Liu Wenshao in the Three Rites and within a year or two had the great principles largely in hand.

s0148.literal: At nineteen, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered an examination on the Correct Meaning of Confucius and the meanings of the Zhou li and Li ji; Ji placed at the top.
s0148.idiomatic: At nineteen, Emperor Wu of Liang examined him on the Correct Meaning of Confucius and the Zhou li and Li ji; Ji placed at the top.

s0149.literal: He was then made Retainer of the Libationer of Yangzhou.
s0149.idiomatic: He was then made retainer of the libationer of Yangzhou.

s0150.literal: He went to Erudite Song Huaifang of the Imperial Academy to question the meaning of the Yi li; Huaifang was a northerner who had brought from Wei commentaries on the Yi li and Li ji, kept secret and not transmitted. When he was about to die he told his family: "After my death, if Student Qi comes, give him the texts of the Yi li and Li ji meanings; if he does not come, bury them with my corpse."
s0150.idiomatic: He went to imperial academy erudite Song Huaifang to question the Yi li; Huaifang was a northerner who had brought Yi li and Li ji commentaries from Wei and kept them secret. When he was dying he told his family, "After my death, if Student Qi comes, give him the Yi li and Li ji texts; if he does not come, bury them with me."

s0151.literal: Such was the esteem in which Confucians held him.
s0151.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which Confucians held him.

s0152.literal: Soon he was additionally made Erudite of the Grand Academy.
s0152.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made erudite of the grand academy.

s0153.literal: When Jianwen was crown prince, he summoned Ji to lecture and discuss.
s0153.idiomatic: When Jianwen was crown prince, he summoned Ji to lecture.

s0154.literal: He also once gave a banquet gathering profound Confucians, first ordering Daoist scholars to question one another, then ordering Central Palace Attendant Xu Chi to range through great principles with sharp talk interspersed.
s0154.idiomatic: He also once gave a banquet for profound Confucians, first ordering Daoist scholars to debate one another, then ordering central palace attendant Xu Chi to range through great principles with sharp talk.

s0155.literal: Chi's rhetoric was fluent and hard to answer; all were overawed and lost their order.
s0155.idiomatic: Chi's rhetoric was fluent and hard to answer; all were overawed and lost their composure.

s0156.literal: Ji then ranged through the meanings [13]; he and Chi went back and forth, Ji spirited and at ease, answering like flowing water; Jianwen deeply admired him.
s0156.idiomatic: Ji then ranged through the meanings [13]; he and Chi debated back and forth, Ji spirited and at ease, answering like flowing water; Jianwen deeply admired him.

s0157.literal: Soon he was made Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, then promoted to Regular Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
s0157.idiomatic: Soon he was made extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry, then promoted to regular extraordinary attendant.

s0158.literal: When Emperor Jing assumed the provisional regime, he went out as Long Marcher of Jiangzhou and followed Shen Tai in garrisoning Southern Yuzhou.
s0158.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing assumed the provisional regime, Ji went out as long marcher of Jiangzhou and followed Shen Tai in garrisoning Southern Yuzhou.

s0159.literal: When Tai fled to Qi he forced Ji to go with him; later Ji escaped back from Ye.
s0159.idiomatic: When Tai fled to Qi he forced Ji to go with him; later Ji escaped back from Ye.

s0160.literal: He again followed Cheng Wenji on the northern campaign; when the armies were destroyed at Lüliang, Ji was captured by Zhou and only after long time returned.
s0160.idiomatic: He again followed Cheng Wenji on the northern campaign; when the armies were destroyed at Lüliang, Ji was captured by Zhou and only after a long time returned.

s0161.literal: He was again made Erudite Assistant of the Imperial Academy and appointed Recorder of the Prince of Shixing's household in the Central Guard.
s0161.idiomatic: He was again made erudite assistant of the imperial academy and appointed recorder of the Prince of Shixing's household in the central guard.

s0162.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Taijian, aged sixty-three.
s0162.idiomatic: He died in year 13 of Taijian, aged sixty-three.

s0163.literal: Ji in the Liang age compiled a Recorded Meaning of the Three Rites; it was lost in the turmoil, but his forty-scroll Meaning of the Li ji circulated in the world.
s0163.idiomatic: Ji in Liang times compiled a Recorded Meaning of the Three Rites, lost in the turmoil; his forty-scroll Meaning of the Li ji circulated in the world.

s0164.literal: Zheng Zhuo, styled Maozhao, was a native of Xin'an in Dongyang.
s0164.idiomatic: Zheng Zhuo, styled Maozhao, was from Xin'an in Dongyang.

s0165.literal: His grandfather Hui was Liang Administrator of Hengyang.
s0165.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was Liang administrator of Hengyang.

s0166.literal: His father Jihui was Regular Attendant of Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry and Magistrate of Jian'an.
s0166.idiomatic: His father Jihui was regular attendant of direct communication of the scattered cavalry and magistrate of Jian'an.

s0167.literal: Zhuo from youth was clever and keen, devoted himself to Confucian learning, and in youth received instruction from Huang Kan.
s0167.idiomatic: Zhuo was clever and keen from youth, devoted himself to Confucian learning, and studied under Huang Kan.

s0168.literal: In the fifth year of Zhongtong of Liang he was first appointed Court Gentleman for the Dynasty.
s0168.idiomatic: In year 5 of Zhongtong of Liang he was first appointed court gentleman for the dynasty.

s0169.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Attendant at the Imperial Banquets, and Recorder of the Prince of Linchuan's household in Pacify-the-East; he was transferred to Recorder of the Prince of Shaoling's household in Pacify-the-West.
s0169.idiomatic: He rose to extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry, attendant at the imperial banquets, and recorder of the Prince of Linchuan's pacify-the-east household, then recorder of the Prince of Shaoling's pacify-the-west household.

s0170.literal: When Jianwen was crown prince he greatly loved the classics and brought Zhuo in as a Meaning Scholar of the Western Secretariat.
s0170.idiomatic: When Jianwen was crown prince he loved the classics and brought Zhuo in as a meaning scholar of the western secretariat.

s0171.literal: In the Chengsheng era he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry and additionally Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
s0171.idiomatic: In the Chengsheng era he was made regular attendant of direct communication and additionally erudite of the imperial academy.

s0172.literal: Soon he was made Martial-Resolution General and additionally Attendant for Palace Affairs of the Secretariat.
s0172.idiomatic: Soon he was made martial-resolution general and additionally attendant for palace affairs of the secretariat.

s0173.literal: In the ages of Gaozu and Shizu he served as Deliberator in the households of the Princes of Linchuan in Pacify-the-East and Poyang in Pacify-the-North, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Palace Gentlemen, and in his former office was additionally Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
s0173.idiomatic: Under Gaozu and Shizu he served as deliberator in the households of the princes of Linchuan and Poyang, rose to grand master of palace gentlemen, and in his former office was additionally erudite of the imperial academy.

s0174.literal: Before he could take the appointment he died in the thirteenth year of Taijian, aged sixty-eight.
s0174.idiomatic: Before he could take the appointment he died in year 13 of Taijian, aged sixty-eight.

s0175.literal: Zhuo by nature was diligent and especially clear in the Three Rites.
s0175.idiomatic: Zhuo was by nature diligent and especially expert in the Three Rites.

s0176.literal: In youth he once dreamed of meeting Huang Kan on the road; Kan said to Zhuo, "Young Master Zheng, open your mouth," and Kan spat into Zhuo's mouth; from then on his grasp of principles advanced further.
s0176.idiomatic: In youth he dreamed of meeting Huang Kan on the road; Kan said, "Young Master Zheng, open your mouth," and spat into Zhuo's mouth; from then on his grasp of principles advanced further.

s0177.literal: Zhuo's family was poor; he copied commentaries day into night, and when brush tips were worn out he would shave them for reuse.
s0177.idiomatic: Zhuo's family was poor; he copied commentaries day into night, and when brush tips wore out he shaved them for reuse.

s0178.literal: Zhuo often ate vegetables; lecturing often brought heart heat; in melon season he would lie down and use melon to calm his heart, then rise and recite at once—such was his devoted will.
s0178.idiomatic: Zhuo often ate vegetables; lecturing often brought heart heat; in melon season he would lie down with melon to calm his heart, then rise and recite at once—such was his devotion.

s0180.literal: At the time there were Zhang Ya of Jinling, Lu Xu of Wu, Shen Dewei of Wuxing, and He Deji of Kuaiji, all styling themselves masters of ritual learning.
s0180.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Ya of Jinling, Lu Xu of Wu, Shen Dewei of Wuxing, and He Deji of Kuaiji all styled themselves masters of ritual learning.

s0181.literal: Lu Xu in youth studied Cui Ling'en's lineage of meaning in the Three Rites; in the Liang age Baekje memorialized requesting an erudite to lecture on the rites, and an edict ordered Xu to go.
s0181.idiomatic: Lu Xu in youth studied Cui Ling'en's lineage of meaning in the Three Rites; in Liang times Baekje requested an erudite to lecture on the rites, and an edict ordered Xu to go.

s0182.literal: On his return he was made Attendant at the Imperial Banquets and Magistrate of Dingyang.
s0182.idiomatic: On his return he was made attendant at the imperial banquets and magistrate of Dingyang.

s0183.literal: At the beginning of Tianjia he attended Prince Bomao of Shixing in study and was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for the Rites Bureau.
s0183.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjia he attended Prince Bomao of Shixing in study and was promoted to director of the masters of writing for the rites bureau.

s0186.literal: He Deji, styled Chengye, transmitted ritual learning through the generations.
s0186.idiomatic: He Deji, styled Chengye, transmitted ritual learning through the generations.

s0187.literal: His grandfather Wenfa and father Yan both served Liang as Directors of the Masters of Writing for the Rites Bureau and were famed in their age.
s0187.idiomatic: His grandfather Wenfa and father Yan both served Liang as directors of the masters of writing for the rites bureau and were famed in their age.

s0188.literal: Deji in youth traveled to study in the capital; for years he did not return, clothing and funds were exhausted, and he was ashamed to wear old and worn garments—in deep winter he wore only a lined jacket and trousers.
s0188.idiomatic: Deji in youth studied in the capital; for years he did not return, his clothing and funds were exhausted, and he was ashamed to wear old garments—in deep winter he wore only a lined jacket and trousers.

s0189.literal: He once met a woman before White Horse Temple whose dress was very splendid; she called Deji into the temple gate and removed her white silk headcloth to give him.
s0189.idiomatic: He once met a woman before White Horse Temple in splendid dress; she called Deji into the temple gate and gave him her white silk headcloth.

s0190.literal: She then said to Deji: "You are about to become a great vessel; soon you will not be poor and cold, so I give you this.
s0190.idiomatic: She then said to Deji, "You are about to become a great vessel; soon you will not be poor and cold, so I give you this.

s0191.literal: " Deji asked the old woman's name; she did not answer and left.
s0191.idiomatic: " Deji asked the old woman's name; she did not answer and left.

s0192.literal: Deji in the Li ji was called penetratingly clear; he lived by transmitting instruction and was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for the Rites Bureau.
s0192.idiomatic: Deji was called penetratingly clear in the Li ji; he lived by teaching and rose to director of the masters of writing for the rites bureau.

s0193.literal: Although Deji did not reach high office, three generations of Confucian learning all held the Rites Bureau, and opinion of the time praised that the line did not fall.
s0193.idiomatic: Although Deji did not reach high office, three generations of Confucian learning all held the rites bureau, and opinion praised that the line did not fall.

s0194.literal: Quan Huan, styled Hongli, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
s0194.idiomatic: Quan Huan, styled Hongli, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

s0195.literal: In youth he received the Changes from Erudite Chu Zhongdu, devoted himself to study and play, and obtained its subtle points.
s0195.idiomatic: In youth he studied the Changes under erudite Chu Zhongdu, devoted himself to study, and obtained its subtle points.

s0196.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing of Liang he served as Gentleman of the Princely Household and Court Gentleman for the Dynasty; soon he was made Erudite Assistant of the Imperial Academy and additionally Director of Meanings, specializing in lecturing on the Odes and Changes.
s0196.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiqing of Liang he served as gentleman of the princely household and court gentleman; soon he was made erudite assistant and additionally director of meanings, specializing in the Odes and Changes.

s0197.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was made Director of the Masters of Writing for the Water Bureau.
s0197.idiomatic: In year 1 of Shaotai he was made director of the masters of writing for the water bureau.

s0198.literal: In the Taijian era he was repeatedly promoted to Deliberator in the Pacify-South household of the Prince of Shixing [14]; he followed the princely establishment to Xiangzhou and died of illness, aged seventy-four.
s0198.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he rose to deliberator in the pacify-south household of the Prince of Shixing [14]; he followed the establishment to Xiangzhou and died of illness, aged seventy-four.

s0199.literal: Huan mastered the Zhou yi, Lao zi, and Zhuang zi; among those who spoke of the arcane he was universally praised.
s0199.idiomatic: Huan mastered the Zhou yi, Lao zi, and Zhuang zi; among those who spoke of the arcane he was universally praised.

s0200.literal: Zhang Ji, styled Zhiyan, was a native of Wucheng in Qinghe.
s0200.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, styled Zhiyan, was from Wucheng in Qinghe.
